text: Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Everton and Chelsea at Goodison Park.
The hosts head into this one on a high after a superb 3-0 win over top-four hopefuls Newcastle United in midweek.
That was Everton's third victory in four matches, enough to lift them out of the relegation zone despite their 10-point deduction for financial breaches.
Without that penalty, the Toffees would be in the top half of the Premier League.
A below-par Chelsea performance away at Manchester United led to a 2-1 defeat in midweek, the Blues' second loss in three matches.
They head to Goodison Park in 10th, though they are level on points with 13th-placed Bournemouth and only five points above Nottingham Forest in 16th.
Sean Dyche makes just the one change from the win over Newcastle.
Seamus Coleman made his return to the senior side after a long-term knee injury against the Magpies but was forced off, and he is absent for this one.
Garner starts in his place, while Pickford is between the sticks despite picking up a knock late on in the midweek triumph.
Onana returns from a calf injury on the bench.
Mauricio Pochettino's team selection is a bold one as he goes with four alterations from the disappointing loss at Old Trafford.
Silva, Colwill, Sterling and Jackson all drop to the bench, with Broja set to make just his third Premier League start of the season.
James returns to captain the side, while Gallagher and Badiashile also come into the starting XI.
The two teams make their way onto the pitch in front of a vociferous Goodison Park crowd.
Can Everton make it three straight victories? We will find out shortly!
The hosts kick us off and we are under way!
SAVE! Pickford is called into action for the first time as Mudryk lays it back to Fernandez on the edge of the box.
The midfielder hits it first time, but Pickford gets down well to make the stop before Fernandez fails to find the target with the rebound.
Everton have won four of their last five home Premier League matches against Chelsea, although they did lose 1-0 last season on the opening day under Frank Lampard.
A sweeping Everton move ends with Harrison whipping a cross into the penalty area, but the delivery isn't accurate enough and cannot find Calvert-Lewin in the box.
Badiashile gets up well to meet a corner from the right, but his looping header only lands on the roof of the net.
Chelsea have looked threatening so far.

Chelsea are looking to win consecutive away Premier League games against Everton for the first time since beating the Toffees at Goodison Park in 2006-07 (3-2 under Jose Mourinho) and 2007-08 (1-0 under Avram Grant).
Broja drives into the box and looks to have flown past Branthwaite, but the centre-back gets back in the nick of time to make a vital last-ditch tackle and divert behind for a corner.
GREAT STOP! A corner is worked short by Chelsea, and the ball comes out to Palmer.
The forward decides to let fly from range, and his powerful shot looks destined for the top corner.
However, Pickford leaps to his right to acrobatically parry away.
The visitors continue to look the more threatening of the two sides.
Gueye goes in the book for a poor challenge on Fernandez.
He went straight through the back of the Argentina international.
London sides have won their last three Premier League away games against Everton – the Toffees haven't lost four in a row at Goodison Park against sides from the capital since April 1993.
Palmer receives a yellow card for simulation after trying to win a penalty by trailing his leg in the box.
Branthwaite didn't bite, and though Palmer did get up and try to play on, the referee blows and issues the Chelsea man a card.
Chelsea have conceded 24 goals in their 15 previous Premier League games this season, their joint most at this stage of a season, along with in 2015-16.
The 194 shots they have faced is their most after 15 games in a season that Opta has on record (since 2003-04).
Neither side has quite been able to kick into top attacking gear yet, though the visitors have looked the more threatening.
Sanchez is yet to make a save between the Chelsea sticks.
WIDE! Everton go close for the first time as Harrison tries the spectacular with a volley.
His acrobatic effort momentarily has Sanchez worried, though the ball eventually flies past the right post.
Dyche will want more of that from his team.
James is forced off through injury and is replaced by Colwill.
The Chelsea captain has had a torrid time of late in terms of his fitness, and both he and Pochettino will be hoping this fresh worry isn't too bad ahead of the busy upcoming schedule.
Caicedo is now struggling in midfield, temporarily dropping to his haunches.
However, it looks like he will try and soldier on.
Branthwaite is down near the touchline after a coming-together with Palmer.
He is receiving treatment, though it appears he will be okay to continue.
Branthwaite is indeed back to his feet, and while the youngster doesn't look entirely comfortable, he will play on.
That will be a huge relief for the home fans.
We have had just three shots in this game and one on target.
It has been far from a thriller at Goodison Park, and both coaches will be demanding more from their teams.
Mudryk injects a bit of much-needed pace into a Chelsea attack by flying down the left and getting past his man.
He fires a cross into the middle, but Broja's shot at the near post flies well wide of the target.
Badiashile and Cucurella both breathe a big sigh of relief as they fail to deal with a long punt upfield.
McNeil races onto it, but the ball gets caught under his feet before the flag eventually goes up for offside.
Dyche is forced into another first-half change as Young limps off for Patterson.
This has been a frustrating outing for the hosts so far.
A corner is cleared, but only to Gallagher.
The midfielder whips a cross back into the Everton box, but though Badiashile wins the first header, none of his team-mates are there to meet the bouncing ball and the hosts clear.
There will be four minutes of additional time at the end of this first half,
Everton's attempts to find a goal before the interval see them win a couple of corners in quick succession, though Chelsea are able to deal with them relatively easily.
Cucurella goes down clutching his face after clashing with Tarkowski ahead of another Everton corner, though the referee sees no wrongdoing and issues no punishment.
HALF-TIME: EVERTON 0-0 CHELSEA
The half-time whistle blows as both teams head back to the changing rooms with the scoreline goalless.

It has not been a thriller at Goodison Park, though Chelsea have probably just about shaded it, Fernandez forcing a decent save out of Pickford early on before the visitors dominated possession for large spells of the half.
Harrison flashed a volley wide for the hosts, who did seem to be improving in the latter stages of the opening 45 minutes.
The first half had just one shot on target, and the teams combined for just 0.34 xG (expected goals).
Both Dyche and Pochettino will think this game is there for the taking if their sides can just find their feet in attack.
Onana makes his return from injury as he comes on for Gueye at half-time.
The visitors get the ball rolling again for the second half.
Everton have now stopped the opposition from scoring a first-half goal in 10 of their 16 games.
Only Aston Villa (11) and Crystal Palace (11) have done this more often in the Premier League this season.
Palmer lays the ball off to Fernandez outside the box, but the midfielder's effort is tame and lacks the power or direction to really trouble Pickford.

text: CLOSE! Everton's first shot on target of the game comes from McNeil, who turns on the edge of the box before lashing goalwards.
His powerful drive is heading for the bottom corner, but Sanchez leaps down to his right to parry wide.
Sanchez goes down temporarily and looks in some discomfort, though he eventually gets back to his feet.
Dyche will be wanting his players to test the Chelsea goalkeeper as soon as possible to take advantage of any problems Sanchez may be having.
GOOOAAALLL!!!!!! DOUCOURE FIRES EVERTON IN FRONT!!! The Toffees catch Chelsea on the counter, and McNeil slides a delightful pass into the path of Calvert-Lewin.
Sanchez races out to close the angle and make the save from Calvert-Lewin's initial effort, but the ball only finds its way to the incoming Doucoure, who rifles into the back of the net.
1-0 to the hosts at Goodison Park!
Everton are unbeaten when scoring the opening goal in the Premier League this season, winning six and drawing two of those games.
Branthwaite goes in the book for catching Broja not far outside the Everton box.
Perhaps more worryingly, Chelsea will have a free-kick in a great shooting position.
While Palmer's free-kick is low and powerful, it's also straight at Pickford, who makes a routine save.
It has just not quite been Palmer's game yet.
Since Dyche's first game as Everton manager in February, Doucoure has more non-penalty goals in the Premier League than any other midfielder (11).
Twenty-five minutes left at Goodison Park, and Everton have their sights firmly set on a fourth win in five Premier League matches.
Chelsea, meanwhile, are staring down the barrel of another defeat.
In an attacking change, Pochettino brings on Sterling for Fernandez.
Sterling, a former Liverpool player, receives a hostile welcome from the home crowd.
Jackson comes on for Broja, who failed to find the target with his only shot during his time on the pitch and struggled to make an impact.
Dyche freshens up his attack, replacing Calvert-Lewin with Beto.
The former Udinese striker netted off the bench against Newcastle and will be looking to make a similar impact here.
Sterling looks to make an immediate impact by getting down the right, but Mykolenko does superbly to win a goal-kick for his side.
The home fans loved that.
Everton manager Sean Dyche has lost his last five home Premier League games against Chelsea, all as Burnley boss.
He could be set to end that poor run here, though.
Mudryk goes in the book for kicking the ball away in frustration after being penalised.

With Chelsea having to throw more bodies forward in their pursuit of an equaliser, there could be opportunities for the likes of Beto and McNeil to get in behind the visitors' defence and catch them on the counter.
Cucurella tries his luck from just outside the box, but his low effort is straight down the throat of Pickford.
Chelsea have desperately lacked that cutting edge in the final third in this game.
Everton hearts are temporarily in mouths as Sterling charges into the box before the ball bounces dangerously around the hosts' box, though Dyche's men are just about able to scramble clear.
Everton may have a lot of defending between now and full-time as they try for another important victory.
Dyche would love a second goal to calm any nerves.
Pochettino is forced into another change.
This time it's between the sticks as Sanchez limps off for Petrovic.
Maatsen also comes on for Cucurella.
Can the young substitute make an impact over these final six or so minutes?
Dyche looks to his bench again, bringing on Dobbin for Harrison.
Chelsea are dominating the ball now, with Everton daring the visitors to try and break them down.
That has rarely looked like happening in this game, though there is still time for Pochettino's men.
There will be seven minutes of additional time for Chelsea to try and find an equaliser.
The home fans certainly didn't want to see that number!
GOOOAAALLL!!!!!! DOBBIN MAKES IT 2-0!!!! Instead of taking a corner short and trying to keep it there, Garner decides to whip it into the box.
It proves to be a great decision as the substitute goalkeeper Petrovic fails to punch clear the delivery, sending it straight into the path of Dobbin.
The youngster sets himself before firing into the back of the net to spark wild celebrations and surely make the points safe for Everton!
That was Dobbin's first ever senior goal for Everton and will be a moment to cherish should the Toffees go on and win this game.
Everton are just moments away now from sealing another valuable three points.
Chelsea, on the other hand, have again been below par.
FULL-TIME: EVERTON 2-0 CHELSEA
The full-time whistle sparks more jubilant Goodison Park celebrations as Everton clinch a 2-0 victory against a disappointing Chelsea side.
The first half was a low-key affair, but Doucoure's 54th-minute goal gave Everton life and something to defend.

They had to do a lot of that, though they rarely looked seriously troubled by the visitors' tame attack, and the points were made safe in added time as 20-year-old substitute Dobbin lashed home for his first senior goal for the club to put the game to bed.
The win extends Everton's gap to the bottom three to four points, and they will look to continue their great form when they travel to struggling Burnley next Saturday.
For Chelsea, another poor performance and results elsewhere mean they drop to 12th, and they will hope to put in a better display when they host relegation-threatened Sheffield United next weekend.
That is all we have from Goodison Park, so thanks for your company and goodbye!
